rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a strong baseline configuration. This experiment tests a multimodal model with advanced RNA (scgpt) and image (imagenet_vit_l) encoders, weighted fusion, and singleprofile setting. It balances exploration by using high-quality encoders while keeping complexity manageable. The expected cost is moderate due to the imagenet_vit_l encoder, which is more expensive than resnet50 but likely to provide better performance than simpler encoders like pca_n2000.

The existing evidence shows that config_002 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, resnet50, weighted fusion) achieves 0.422 accuracy. This experiment tests a simpler RNA encoder (pca_n2000) in the same setup, which reduces uncertainty about the RNA encoder's impact on performance. It is cheaper (estimated lower GPU hours than config_002) and clarifies whether a simpler encoder can match or exceed the current accuracy, balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal singleprofile with pca_n2000+resnet50) achieves 0.523 accuracy at 0.87 GPU hours. Testing config_020 (same RNA/image encoders but multiprofile with avgpool aggregation) clarifies if multiprofile improves performance while maintaining similar cost. This balances exploitation of the current best configuration's components with exploration of profile settings, which may yield higher accuracy. Expected cost is ~0.9 GPU hours.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings (config_020) achieve the highest accuracy (0.639) so far. This experiment tests a similar multiprofile setup with scgpt RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder, which could validate if RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance. It maintains avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (proven effective in config_020) while using scgpt (more expressive than pca_n2000). Expected cost is similar to config_020 (10.6 GPU hours), but with potential for higher accuracy. This balances exploitation of multiprofile success with exploration of RNA encoder variations.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with pca_n2000 and resnet50 (config_020) achieve the highest accuracy (0.639) so far. This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation in the same RNA/image encoder combination, which could capture more complex interactions. The transformer aggregation is expected to be more expensive (~8 GPU hours) but offers a logical extension of the current top-performing configuration, balancing exploration and exploitation while staying within the budget.

The existing evidence shows config_020 (multiprofile, pca_n2000+resnet50, avgpool+weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.639) but uses older encoders. This experiment tests replacing RNA encoder with scgpt and image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (more advanced models) while keeping avgpool+weighted fusion. It clarifies if better encoders can surpass config_020's accuracy. Expected cost ~12-13 GPU hours (higher than config_020's 10.6), but the potential for significant accuracy improvement justifies the cost given the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows config_020 (multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.639) but at high cost (10.60 GPU hours). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders and aggregation method but uses concat fusion instead of weighted, clarifying if fusion method impacts performance. It balances exploitation of promising components (pca_n2000/resnet50/avgpool) with exploration of fusion alternatives. Expected cost is similar to config_020 but with lower complexity, making it a cost-effective way to validate the current best configuration's components.

The current best accuracy (0.639) is achieved by config_020 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted). Testing config_047 (same aggregation/fusion but with imagenet_vit_l image encoder) explores whether a more powerful image encoder improves accuracy. This balances exploitation (building on the current best's architecture) and exploration (testing a stronger image encoder). The expected cost is ~15 GPU hours, which is manageable within the remaining budget, and could yield higher accuracy than the current best.

The existing evidence shows that config_020 (pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6389). This experiment tests whether using a more powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of combining advanced image encoders with complex aggregation methods, which are critical for multimodal tasks. Despite higher cost, this is the best use of the final experiment to potentially surpass the current best.

The existing evidence shows config_020 (0.639 accuracy) and config_047 (0.635 accuracy) are the top performers. config_027 uses the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000) and image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) as config_047 but switches to concat fusion, which might improve accuracy by leveraging richer interaction patterns. This experiment tests whether concat fusion outperforms weighted fusion for this encoder combination. It is the best use of the final budget as it targets a critical design choice (fusion method) with high potential to improve accuracy without excessive cost.
